exposure: Maternal angiogenic factors (PlGF, sFlt-1, sFlt-1/PlGF ratio)
outcome: Adverse perinatal outcome (composite of emergency Cesarean section for non-reassuring fetal status, metabolic acidosis, neonatal unit admission, and/or perinatal death)
cohort: The study included women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with late-onset fetal smallness and a gestational age of >= 34 weeks at delivery.
finding: Combining the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio with estimated fetal weight (EFW) and Doppler criteria offers the highest detection rate for adverse perinatal outcome and may help identify imminent pre-eclampsia in pregnancies with fetal smallness.
mod_finding: One component of the composite adverse perinatal outcome was emergency Cesarean section for non-reassuring fetal status.
